subject: Reserved Pool Proposal — multi-workload sizing & discount tiers
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@lumahealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Estimating reserved pool for Q1 workloads

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the demo last week — the throughput looked promising. Our procurement team asked me to get an initial sizing and cost estimate for a reserved GPU pool that would cover two primary workloads: (1) patient-chat (mostly short context, high concurrency), and (2) document extraction (longer context, batch jobs).

Rough forecast (per day):
- Patient-chat: 120k requests/day, avg context 512 tokens, peak concurrency ~320
- Doc-extract: 18k jobs/day, avg context 6k tokens, processed in batches (avg batch size 12)

Goal: predictable monthly spend with a throughput SLO for peak hours. We also expect to run a small canary of a new LLM variant at 10% of traffic.

Can you advise on recommended GPU pool sizing, baseline throughput guarantees, and what a realistic reserved commit looks like for this profile? Procurement will want clear discount tiers for a 12-month commit.

Appreciate it — Sam
Luma Health

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@lumahealth.com>, procurement@lumahealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Estimating reserved pool for Q1 workloads

Sam — thanks for the detail, this is a great starting point. I've attached a short spreadsheet template so we can lock down assumptions (tokenization variance, concurrency windows). A few quick clarifying Qs before Ben and I run simulations: 

1) What percent of patient-chat requests are expected to be streaming vs full-response? (streaming increases open-shard duration)
2) For doc-extract, is the 6k token context the average per job after concatenation or before chunking?
3) Do you expect both workloads to be active in the same region (US-WEST) or split?

Ben — can you run a couple of pool-sizing scenarios (optimistic / expected / conservative) and include recommended fallback variants and quantization notes? Also include: per-token cost estimate, per-hour throughput guarantees, and suggested discount tiers for a 12-month reserved commit.

Next step: once we align the numbers, I'll share a one-page proposal for procurement.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Sam Patel <sam@lumahealth.com>, procurement@lumahealth.com
Date: 2026-12-08T08:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Estimating reserved pool for Q1 workloads

On Tue, Dec 7, 2026 at 11:05 AM Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ben — can you run a couple of pool-sizing scenarios (optimistic / expected / conservative)...

Folks — ran workload sims based on the attached forecast (I used 70% streaming for patient-chat and treated doc-extract as batched inference with KV caching disabled between jobs). Key assumptions are in the spreadsheet. Highlights below: 

- Expected scenario (recommended starting point):
  * GPU pool: 8x A100-80GB equiv. (mixed with 2x smaller instances for canary routing)
  * Steady throughput: ~1,200 tokens/sec sustained for chat across the pool (burst to 3k tokens/sec for short peaks)
  * Doc-extract: efficient batching yields ~220 jobs/hr per GPU during batch windows (avg latency per job ~40s)
  * Peak concurrency coverage: patient-chat 320 concurrent sessions covered with 20–25% headroom

- Optimistic: 6x A100 equiv (assumes 40% traffic reduction via prefix-caching, more aggressive quantization)
- Conservative: 12x A100 equiv (accounts for higher-than-expected streaming hold-open time and model drift)

Pricing / reserved commit guidance (12-month):
- List commit (baseline unit): $X/hour per A100-equivalent (placeholder — procurement requested ranges; we'll convert to monthly in proposal)
- Discount tiers (examples): 10% @ 6k committed GPU-hours/mo; 18% @ 12k committed GPU-hours/mo; 25% @ 24k committed GPU-hours/mo.
- SLA/throughput guarantees: we can commit to 99.5% pool availability and a regional failover policy. Throughput guarantees tied to model family + input distribution in SLA appendix.

Operational notes:
- Canary routing: route 10% traffic to separate lightweight nodes to limit tail risk; those nodes can be lower-spec and excluded from commit calculation if desired.
- Autoscaling: burst to cloud on detected saturation (cost pass-through), or absorb with reserved buffer depending on purchase.

I'll attach the simulation output and a slide with per-tokenized cost ranges. Happy to walk through numbers.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Attachment: luma_multiworkload_forecast_q4-q1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Sam Patel <sam@lumahealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-08T14:16:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Estimating reserved pool for Q1 workloads

Looping in a manager note on pricing — given Luma's forecast and willingness for a 12-month commit, we can be flexible on structure. A few suggestions: 

1) Offer a blended commit: count canary nodes as "non-committed" to protect Luma while keeping most capacity reserved.
2) Front-load a 3-month price incentive (additional 5% credit on first 90 days) to smooth migration and defray integration costs.
3) Provide a 30-day break clause tied to SLA misses (mutually defined metrics) for the first year to reduce procurement friction.

If procurement pushes back on percent discounts, provide a structured negotiation sheet: deeper discounts in exchange for longer payment terms or higher committed hours. Jasmine — you can lead procurement touchpoint and we can fast-track a term sheet if they give a go-ahead.

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
VP, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@lumahealth.com>, procurement@lumahealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-09T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Reserved Pool Proposal — multi-workload sizing & discount tiers (proposal attached)

Sam — thanks for the quick turnaround, and thanks Ben/Aditya for the input. Attached is a one-page proposal (PDF) and the forecast workbook. High level summary: 

- Recommended starting commitment: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (expected scenario). This covers your steady-state patient-chat load with ~25% headroom and handles doc-extract batch windows without added latency.
- Canary: 2x smaller nodes, run at 10% traffic and excluded from committed-hours calculation.
- Pricing: example discount tiers for a 12-month reserved contract — 12% effective discount at the 12k GPU-hours/mo band; 20% for 24k GPU-hours/mo. We included a 5% onboarding credit applied over the first 90 days.
- SLA & Guarantees: 99.5% pool availability; regional failover plan; throughput guarantees in appendix tied to model-version and test-set.
- Next steps:
  1) Confirm whether canary nodes should be excluded from the commit calculation (yes/no).
  2) Procurement to review the attached term sheet and indicate desired discount band and payment cadence.
  3) We'll schedule a 30-min pricing review with Ben to walk the simulation outputs.

If procurement wants an alternative structure (monthly ramp vs flat commit), we can model that quickly. Let me know best time for the review this week.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: proposed_reserved_pricing_breakdown.pdf, luma_multiworkload_forecast_q4-q1.xlsx
